## Module Overview

### Module summary

caribou_SSUD maps caribou habitat use from an integrated step-selection analysis (iSSA).
It turns the model's fixed-effect coefficients into a steady-state utilization distribution [@PottsSchlagel2020]: the long-run density of use the model's habitat and movement terms imply over a landscape.
The result is a probability density of use (PDE) for each model, normalized to sum to 1 over the area it is predicted for, and a binned map of it (`pdeMap`) that compares the cells within that area.

This module currently handles two caribou ecotypes (`ecotype`): northern mountain caribou (NMC), whose coefficients are read from the fixed-effect table of a fitted model, and boreal caribou, whose `glmmTMB` models are supplied one per jurisdiction.
With `simulationScale` it maps the global model, one model per region, or both.

In static mode (`simulationProcess = "static"`, the default) it maps the baseline landscape only.
In dynamic mode it also rebuilds the landscape layers that change during a simulation every `predictionInterval` years from `predictStartYear`, and maps habitat use on each.
Each layer is matched by its name to what forecasts it (`dynamicLayers`):

- forest cover (NMC: `prop_forest_240`, `prop_forest_1200`; boreal: `prop_needleleaf`, `prop_mixedforest`), from the simulated tree cohorts (LandR);
- time since fire (NMC: `ts_fire_240`, `ts_fire_1200`; boreal: `timeSinceFire`), from the simulated fires (e.g. `scfm`);
- time since harvest (NMC: `ts_harv_240`; boreal: `timeSinceHarvest`), which only ages for now, as no module is integrated to simulate harvest yet;
- distance to human disturbance (NMC: e.g. `dist_paved_240`; boreal: e.g. `distpaved`), from the roads and mines `anthroDisturbance_Generator` adds. This is only set up for NMC in Yukon at this time; boreal distances stay as in `modelLand`.

Every other layer (e.g. NMC's land cover, boreal's `prop_veg` and `prop_wets`) stays as in `modelLand`.
If part of the model, layers keep the resolution in their names: a coarser layer (e.g. NMC's 1200 m layers on a 240 m grid) is built from the grid's cells, as the model's layers were.
A layer with no resolution in its name (e.g. the boreal layers) is on the simulation's grid.

For a model fit with seasons (terms such as `seasonwinter:prop_forest_240_end`; currently NMC only), the module makes a map for each season (`seasonMaps`) and a full-year map that combines them, weighted by season length or as chosen (`fullYear`, `seasonWeights`).

### Module inputs and parameters

The module needs the model and the landscape the model reads (Table \@ref(tab:moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD)):

- `iSSAmodels`, the models, named `global` and/or by region (e.g. `NT`). Each can be the fitted model (`glmmTMB`) or a table of its fixed-effect coefficients (columns `term` and `estimate`, as in hsaCEtool's `<model>_fixed.csv`), for either ecotype.
  If not supplied, the NMC global model's table is read from `<coefficientsModel>_fixed.csv` in the model's zip file in the Google Drive folder `modelsFolderID`, and boreal models from `iSSAmodels.RData` in `outputFolderID`.
  (`iSSAcoefficients`, one table for the global model, still works but is deprecated.)
- For a model with seasons (NMC), `iSSAseasons`, the days in each season, used to weight the full-year map; read from the model's zip file when it has one.
- `modelLand`, the landscape layers, named as in the model's terms; a layer the model needs and the list lacks stops the run, naming it.
  For NMC, distances capped for the model (more than 20 km set to 21 km) carry `_adj` in their names (e.g. `dist_paved_240_adj`); the boreal distances are not capped.
- `studyAreaCaribou`, the area the global model was fit on, and, for the regional models, `studyArea_juris`, one area per region.
  Optionally, `studyAreaReporting`, an area to normalize and bin the maps over instead (see `pdeArea`).
- Optionally, a baseline made earlier (`pde` and `pdeMap`, or a folder, zip file or URL in `baselineSource`), so the baseline is read rather than made again.

In dynamic mode it also uses, from the other modules of the simulation:

- the simulated forest (`cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`, with `sppEquiv` to tell conifers from broadleaf species);
- the time since fire (`timeSinceFire`): only fires burned in the simulation (from `baselineYear` on) are read from it, so a map that starts from stand age is not read as fire history;
- the human disturbance (`disturbanceList`);
- the simulation's grid (`rasterToMatch`), which every `modelLand` layer must match. If the model
  has layers coarser than the grid's cells, the grid's top-left corner must also be a multiple of
  each of those resolutions. A template cropped to a study area should be snapped outward to the
  coarsest template resolution, not just the model's (e.g. 4800 m on the NMC templates, though the
  current NMC models go up to 1200 m), so later models with coarser layers fit too.

A forecaster that is missing leaves its layers as they are: fire and harvest layers only age, and distances stay as in `modelLand`.

```{r moduleInputs-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_inputs <- SpaDES.core::moduleInputs("caribou_SSUD", "..")
knitr::kable(df_inputs,
             caption = "List of (ref:caribou-SSUD) input objects and their description.")
```

The parameters (Table \@ref(tab:moduleParams-caribou-SSUD)) choose the ecotype, the models and the area each is mapped over (`ecotype`, `simulationScale`, `pdeArea`), static or dynamic mode and the prediction years (`simulationProcess`, `predictStartYear`, `predictionInterval`, `predictLastYear`), and where the model and a premade baseline come from (`coefficientsModel`, `modelsFolderID`, `baselineSource`).
In dynamic mode, further parameters say how each forecast layer is built; set them to match how the model's layers were made:

- all layers: `dynamicLayers` (which layers are forecast, and from what; each ecotype has its own default, matching the layer names above) and `baselineYear` (the year `modelLand` describes, and the simulation should start in: 2025 for the NMC `modelLand`, 2022 for the boreal NWT one);
- forest: `forestForecast` (`"change"`, the default, adds the simulated change since the start to `modelLand`'s layer; `"LandR"` uses the simulated forest alone), `forestTypes` (the LandR forest types each layer counts: NMC `prop_forest` counts all forest; boreal `prop_needleleaf` counts conifer stands and `prop_mixedforest` deciduous and mixed ones) and `forestMinBiomass`;
- moving windows: `movingWindow` (the circles forecast layers are averaged in, as the model's layers were built: one row per window, a pattern on layer names and a radius in m; by default NMC's 240 m land cover in 500 m; for the boreal NWT `modelLand` use `data.frame(layers = "^prop_(needleleaf|mixedforest)$", radius = 720)`). A radius of `NA` takes the input `buffer`, the radius other modules in the workflow use (e.g. prepTracks); a different radius stops, so the modules cannot disagree. Only forest layers take a window so far;
- time since fire and harvest: `ts_else` (the value given to cells that never burned or were never harvested; 200 for the NMC models), `noEventYear` (for a `modelLand` that counts such cells from a stand-in year instead: the boreal NWT one counts them from 1900, so use `list(fire = 1900, harvest = 1900)`), and `fireCoarse` and `harvestCoarse` (for layers coarser than the grid, such as NMC's 1200 m layers: whether they take the mean, the default, or the most recent fire or harvest year of their cells; use the rule the model was fit with: the mean for the V2 NMC models such as `fullV2_to2020`, the most recent for the earlier ones);
- distances (NMC): `disturbanceClasses` (which `anthroDisturbance_Generator` classes each distance is measured to; set by default for NMC in Yukon, none for boreal), `distanceCellSize` (the cell size distances are measured on, 30 m by default, as for the NMC model's layers) and `distanceCap` (the cap for `_adj` layers).


```{r moduleParams-caribou-SSUD, echo = FALSE, eval = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
df_params <- SpaDES.core::moduleParams("caribou_SSUD", "..")
```

### Events

- `init`: makes the baseline PDE and map for the current landscape, or reads a premade one, and saves a baseline it made to the output folder.
  In dynamic mode it also schedules the two events below, from `predictStartYear` every `predictionInterval` years, and in the last year when `predictLastYear` is `TRUE`.
- `simLayers` (dynamic mode): rebuilds the layers that change, on top of the layers that do not (`fixedSSUD`), and writes the stack:
  - forest cover: the simulated cohorts classed into forest types, as a share of each cell at the layer's resolution (and of a circle around it, for layers `movingWindow` picks);
  - time since fire: the most recent of `modelLand`'s fire and the simulation's, in years; cells that never burned get `ts_else` (NMC) or keep counting from `noEventYear` (boreal NWT);
  - time since harvest: `modelLand`'s, aged to the year;
  - distances (NMC): the smaller of `modelLand`'s distance and the distance to the simulated features of that class, so features outside the simulated area, or of classes the simulation does not add, still count; `_adj` layers are capped again. Distances with no class in `disturbanceClasses` (all boreal ones) stay as in `modelLand`.
- `calcSimPde` (dynamic mode): maps habitat use on the rebuilt layers with the same models as the baseline, into `simPde` and `simPdeMap`, and writes them.

### Plotting

The module does not plot.

### Saving

A baseline the module makes is written to `pde_<.studyAreaName>/` in the output folder, as `pde_<model>.tif` and, when `normalizePDE` is `TRUE`, `pdeMap_<model>.tif`; each file is registered as an output.
The model is `global` or a region (e.g. `pde_global.tif`, or `pde_NT.tif` for a boreal regional model).
For a model with seasons (NMC), a season's maps are named `<model>_<season>` (e.g. `pde_global_winter.tif`), and the full-year map as the model.
In dynamic mode, each prediction year's layers and maps go to its `sims/` subfolder, with the year in their names (e.g. `pde_global_year2030.tif`).

### Links to other modules

In dynamic mode, for both ecotypes, the simulated forest comes from the LandR Biomass modules ([`Biomass_borealDataPrep`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_borealDataPrep), [`Biomass_core`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_core): `cohortData` and `pixelGroupMap`; [`Biomass_regeneration`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/Biomass_regeneration)), and the time since fire from the fire model ([`scfm`](https://github.com/PredictiveEcology/scfm)'s `scfmSpread`: `timeSinceFire`).

Where the model and the landscape come from currently differs by ecotype:

- NMC: the iSSA is fit, and its landscape layers (`modelLand`) and coefficients made, outside SpaDES with [`hsaCEtool`](https://github.com/JWTurn/hsaCEtool).
  In dynamic mode, the human disturbance comes from [`anthroDisturbance_Generator`](https://github.com/FOR-CAST/anthroDisturbance_Generator) (`disturbanceList`).
- Boreal: the iSSA is fit within SpaDES, by a chain of modules: [`caribouLocPrep`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/caribouLocPrep) (cleans the collar locations and makes the study areas, `studyAreaCaribou` and `studyArea_juris`), [`prepTracks`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/prepTracks) (makes the steps), [`prepLandscape`](https://github.com/JWTurn/prepLandscape) (makes the yearly landscape layers), [`extractLand`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/extractLand) (extracts the layers at the steps) and [`caribouiSSA`](https://github.com/gc-rmcinnes/caribouiSSA) (fits the `glmmTMB` models, `iSSAmodels`, and hands on the landscape they read, `modelLand`).
  Distances to human disturbance are not forecast yet.
